//: Mutation matrix for the SCAN AND MODEL half of cue sheets (issue #196, part 3) — the half probe_cuesheet cannot reach, because it is about what a folder on a disk turns into. Two of these are the ones worth naming. `cue-out-of-the-cache-key` is the failure a probe would never notice by accident: editing a .cue does not touch the audio file, so an entry keyed on the audio alone shows yesterday's track list forever and looks like the parser is broken. `sheet-overrules-the-tag` is the opposite mistake — a ripper's guess winning over what the person who tagged the file actually wrote. Driven by native/tools/mutate.py (never a hand-rolled loop; see CONTRIBUTING).

mutants.//: THE ONE A GREEN SUITE WOULD OTHERWISE HIDE. Editing the sidecar changes neither the audio file's mtime nor its size, so without this the album keeps the track list it was first scanned with, forever.
mutants.name: cue-out-of-the-cache-key
mutants.find:
if (cached != known.constEnd() && cached->mtime == mtime && cached->size == size
            && cached->cuePath == cuePath && cached->cueMtime == cueMtime && cached->cueSize == cueSize)
mutants.replace: if (cached != known.constEnd() && cached->mtime == mtime && cached->size == size)

mutants.//: The expansion itself: one file, one row, and the album is the seventy-minute item again.
mutants.name: cue-album-never-expands

mutants.//: Every cue track pointing at the same string. The queue can then hold five entries it cannot tell apart, 'start at track 3' starts at track 1, and each one plays the whole album.
mutants.name: cue-tracks-share-one-path

mutants.//: Cover extraction reaching for the clip url instead of the file. AudioTags cannot open 'edl://…', so a cue album loses its artwork.
mutants.name: cover-read-from-the-clip-url

mutants.//: The browse half of the same expansion: an album row that opens onto ONE seventy-minute leaf again. Run against probe_musicbrowse because what it breaks is what reaches the screen.
mutants.name: cue-album-never-expands-on-screen

mutants.//: Every row reporting the FILE's length: a three-track album of 5:02, 4:09 and 0:00 shows as three five-minute tracks.
mutants.name: cue-track-duration-is-the-file

mutants.//: A sheet whose times overrun its file is a real thing. Without the clamp the last track reports a NEGATIVE length, which every duration formatter downstream renders as nonsense.
mutants.name: negative-last-track-length

mutants.//: Counts following the FILES instead of the rows: a twelve-track album subtitled '1 track', describing the disk rather than the record.
mutants.name: counts-follow-files-not-rows

mutants.//: TAGS WIN. A ripper's guess overruling what the person who tagged the file wrote — the album quietly renames itself to whatever the sheet says.
mutants.name: sheet-overrules-the-tag

mutants.//: …and the other direction: no fallback at all, so an untagged single-file rip stays 'Unknown Artist' with an album named after its folder while the sheet two inches away spells both out.
mutants.name: sheet-fills-in-nothing

mutants.//: The embedded CUESHEET tag ignored: every EAC-descended FLAC rip that carries its sheet inside the file goes back to being one track.
mutants.name: embedded-cuesheet-ignored
mutants.replace: const CueSheet::Sheet sheet = cuePath.isEmpty() ? CueSheet::Sheet{} : sheetFor(cuePath);

mutants.//: …and the precedence between the two, reversed: the baked-in sheet beating the one the user can actually edit.
mutants.name: embedded-beats-the-sidecar
mutants.replace:
const CueSheet::Sheet sheet = !t.cuesheet.isEmpty() ? CueSheet::parse(t.cuesheet)
                                    : (cuePath.isEmpty() ? CueSheet::Sheet{} : sheetFor(cuePath));

mutants.//: A cue claiming any file in its folder. The neighbour of a sheet pointing at something that is no longer on the disk inherits somebody else's track list.
mutants.name: cue-claims-any-neighbour

mutants.//: THE COMPATIBILITY CLAIM. Writing the cue keys unconditionally grows every entry of every ordinary library with three fields that say nothing — the thing the whole increment promises not to do.
mutants.name: ordinary-entries-grow-cue-keys

mutants.//: The open-ended last track lost in the round trip: after a cold start it ends at millisecond zero instead of at the end of the file.
mutants.name: open-ended-last-track-lost-on-load

mutants.//: The parse stamp not moving: every library already scanned keeps its single-file rips as one track until each of those files is edited by hand.
mutants.name: parse-stamp-not-bumped
